lesson_title: Buy Now, Pay Later: What It Really Costs
hook_text: Only R650 a month for a R6 000 television sounds great. Let's do the maths.
clip_script: A television costs R6 000 cash. Or, says the sign, just R650 a month! Twelve payments of R650. Add it up: R7 800. You pay R1 800 extra just to have it now. Save R500 a month instead, and in a year you buy it for cash and keep the R1 800. That is the hidden cost of credit. South Africa has a law to protect you: the National Credit Act. Before you sign, the lender must show you the full cost in plain language. They must check that you can actually afford it. Lending to someone who clearly cannot pay is reckless lending, and a court can cancel it. You get a free credit report every year to check your record. But you have a job too: tell the truth, read before you sign, and pay on time. Credit for a house or your studies can build your future. Credit for things that are gone next month just builds debt.
visual_style: A price tag flipping from R650 to a growing stack of twelve coins totalling R7 800, a balance scale with cash and credit, and a simple shield icon labelled National Credit Act.
pacing: A punchy reveal of the total, a steady rights segment, a firm closing contrast.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and calculate the cost of credit on a real advert.
